items.stem:
Consider the following statements about the era of coalitions:
I. Coalition politics shifted the focus of parties from ideological differences to power-sharing arrangements.
II. The United Front government was supported from outside by the Congress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.answer: Both I and II
items.markingKey: (c) I is correct. II is correct.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The Mandal issue changed Indian politics.
Reason (R): The Mandal Commission recommended 50 per cent reservation for OBCs.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: It recommended 27 per cent.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on emerging consensus and politics since 2014 and answer the questions that follow.
"Political alliances are increasingly based on pragmatic considerations rather than ideology. Most parties accept the political and social claims of the backward castes. Most political parties agree on the new economic policies, though they differ on details."
(i) Who became Prime Minister after the 2014 Lok Sabha elections? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'emerging consensus' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Political alliances in recent decades are based on pragmatism. (2)
items.answer: (i) Narendra Modi (ii) The agreement among most parties since the 1990s on economic policies, OBC reservation, the role of state parties and pragmatic alliances. (iii) Parties prioritise power-sharing over ideology to form governments.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) Narendra Modi (ii) The agreement among most parties since the 1990s on economic policies, OBC reservation, the role of state parties and pragmatic alliances. (iii) Parties prioritise power-sharing over ideology to form governments.

items.stem: Which one of the following statements about the era of coalitions is NOT correct?
items.answer: The UPA was led by the BJP.
items.markingKey: (c) It is incorrect. The UPA was led by the Congress; the NDA was led by the BJP.
options: From 1989 to 2014 no single party won a clear majority in the Lok Sabha.

items.stem:
Read the following extract on the era of coalitions and answer the questions that follow.
"From 1989 to 2014 no single party won a clear majority in the Lok Sabha. In 1996 the BJP emerged as the largest party, and Vajpayee's government lasted only thirteen days. Coalition politics shifted the focus of parties from ideological differences to power-sharing arrangements."
(i) Who led the National Front government formed in 1989? (1)
(ii) Explain the term 'National Front' as it relates to this theme. (1)
(iii) Explain the reason behind the following: Regional parties became important at the Centre. (2)
items.answer: (i) V.P. Singh (ii) The coalition led by V.P. Singh that formed the government in 1989 with outside support of the BJP and the Left. (iii) Coalition governments depended on their support.
items.markingKey: 1+1+2 marks: (i) V.P. Singh (ii) The coalition led by V.P. Singh that formed the government in 1989 with outside support of the BJP and the Left. (iii) Coalition governments depended on their support.
